messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test fails because when calling commandLine.getOptionValue("debug"), the return value is null, contrary to the expectation that it should return the argument value associated with the long option "debug".

Analyzing the CommandLine.getOptionValue(String) method shows it internally calls getOptionValues(String) and returns the first value if non-null. The getOptionValues(String) method first strips leading hyphens from the option name, then looks up keys in the "names" map to translate aliases. If a mapping is found, it uses the mapped "key" to retrieve the corresponding Option object from the "options" map and returns its values.

The key to understand is what keys are available in "names" and "options". The Options.addOption(Option) method, which was called during test setup, adds the Option object keyed by Option.getKey() to the internal maps. The getKey() method returns the short option character if defined (in this case 'd'), or the long option name if no short option is set.

Since in the test the Option was created with short option 'd' and long option "debug", the Option's key is the short option 'd'. Thus, the Options collection holds the option with key 'd'. The "names" map holds mappings from alternate names pointing to this canonical key.

When getOptionValues("debug") is called, it strips hyphens, then in the "names" map looks for "debug" key. This lookup fails since "debug" is not a name key mapping, so the code uses "debug" as the key directly. Since "debug" is not the option key in "options" (which has 'd'), the lookup fails and returns null.

However, calling getOptionValue('d') works because 'd' is the key present in "options" and "names".

Hence, the cause of the bug is that the long option name "debug" is not mapped in the "names" dictionary to the short option key 'd', so lookups by long option name fail. The Option object is only added under its short option key, but not linked in the names map for the long option.

This behavior is contrary to the documentation and expectation that both short and long option names can be used interchangeably. The missing mapping or linking of long option names to option keys in CommandLine causes getOptionValue(String) called with a long option name to fail.

In summary, the failure is due to inconsistent or missing resolution of option keys for long option names in CommandLine.getOptionValues(String), resulting in getOptionValue(longOpt) returning null.

This matches the current bug report summary that getOptionValue behaves contrary to docs for long option names.

No recent bug reports were present to consider.

Suggested fix should focus on ensuring that long option names resolve correctly to option keys in CommandLine.getOptionValues.

The failing test clearly demonstrates that getOptionValue("debug") returns null because "debug" is not found as a key or alias mapping to the underlying option keyed by 'd'.

---
